notes:
A clean five-rung ladder that only needed two judgements. First, bullet 4 is two things at once -- examining the Colorful Door and then fighting through the BCNM it opens -- so it splits, and both bullet numbers ride on the fight because bullet 5 is what says the waves end. All six sub-bullets under bullet 4 are strategy (buffs stripped on entry, Trusts allowed, Yagudo have low HP so bring AoE, Valaineral tanks well) and none is a step. Second, the BCNM instance is never named, so the fight step gets a null zone rather than a guessed one; the only monster the page names anywhere is Laa Yaku the Austere, and it hedges even that with 'generally', so the waves themselves go unrecorded rather than invented.

The Fort Key is step 3's evidence and step 4's requirement -- the page's own sub-bullet says Rotih Moalghett will hand out a replacement if you lose the battle, which both confirms the door eats it and means holding one is not proof you have not already fought. The line after the horizontal rule, about returning to Cait Sith (Mission) for Wings of the Goddess missions, belongs to the mission line and not to this quest.

Splitting them would put two consecutive unmarkable rungs on one object for no gain, and only the second click is observable anyway.

The two key items are the whole ladder: the fluid proves you accepted, the bottle proves you infused. The page itself warns that the bottle arrives silently -- 'you will have no indication of this' -- which is exactly the case where an evidence latch beats the game's own feedback.

The unnumbered line above bullet 1 is a cooldown, not a step: one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet per Vana'dielian day across every Abyssea area, which nothing in the packets reports. The three sub-bullets under bullet 3 explain the 1 / 2 / 5 yalm distances and the sub-bullet under bullet 5 is the reward scale; none is a step. Fame 'avun' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only raw is kept.

notes:
Six bullets, three rungs, and the interesting call is which bullets are not steps. Bullet 2 is the OUTCOME of bullet 1 -- Ramua hands over the checklist and a Hatchet in the same conversation -- so it is not a second visit; it merges, and the Timber survey checklist becomes step 1's evidence. Bullet 4 is a tutorial on how harvesting works for a player who has never done it, and it is also the only place the page names the thing you actually interact with, so it merges into the logging step rather than becoming a rung. Bullet 5 is explicitly optional Records of Eminence advice about sparks and free hatchets and is not part of the quest at all.

The five logs are one step, not five: the page gives them as a flat list with no order, no per-log location and no grid -- the sites are only marked on the wiki's map image, which the prose does not reproduce -- so five zone-less rungs on the same Logging Point in the same zone would be five identical unmarkable copies. As one step they carry a five-item AND-list as evidence, which is exactly the shape the page's After-the-walkthrough Notes describes: the checklist records each log as you take it, and bullet 6 has you hand all five over together.

That same Notes section adds the real constraint -- the logs must be harvested by you, not bought from a shop or the auction house -- so there is no items_alt here. The Woodworking Guild membership in bullet 1's sub-bullet is a genuine gate with no slot in the schema and no observable predicate; Guild Master: Cheupirudaux at (F-3) is where you fix it, but joining a craft guild is not a rung of this quest, so it is flagged and noted rather than made a step.

notes:
The whole middle of this walkthrough is a table, and it is a real one: five empty test tubes going out, five filled ones coming back, each tied to a specific pond. That makes it the best kind of group -- five members, no stated order, each with its own zone and grid and its own distinct key item, so each carries its own evidence and none is duplicated. Four ponds are in Wajaom Woodlands and the fifth is in Bhaflau Thickets; one step, one zone, so they keep their own zones inside the group.

The ponds themselves are never named. The page says only 'visit various ponds', so the target is none rather than a guessed ??? and the kind is obtain rather than examine -- the page does not say what you click, only what you end up holding.

Bullet 1 is written from AFTER acceptance ('After accepting the quest, talk to Nafiwaa'), so the acceptance conversation with Abquhbah is a real first rung that the prose skips over; it is recorded from the same bullet. Bullet 2's opening clause is the outcome of the Nafiwaa visit, so the five empty tubes are that step's evidence. Bullet 4 is the mixing minigame's answer key, not a trip, so it folds into the return to Nafiwaa. Bullet 6 is the closing dialogue choice inside bullet 5's cutscene, so those two merge too.

Two gates cannot be modelled: 'Complete 25 points worth of Assaults as Superior Private' has no slot and no observable predicate, and bullet 5's game-day-plus-a-zoning wait is invisible to the addon. The header writes Abquhbah's grid as '(1-10)' -- a digit typed for the letter I -- and it is recorded as I-10 with the header string kept verbatim in raw.

notes:
Twelve bullets and the first five are a genuine ping-pong between two NPCs standing a few grids apart -- Abquhbah, Hagakoff, Abquhbah, Hagakoff, Abquhbah. That really is what the page says, so it really is five rungs; no two consecutive rungs land on the same NPC, so it is five distinct markers. Nothing in that run is observable, so the mark walks it on the session latch alone.

The mushroom half is where the confidence goes. The page calls the things you click 'the mushroom patch' in lower-case running prose and never names them -- the 'the baskets' case from the hard rules exactly -- so the three mushroom steps carry no target at all. The rungs and their grids are kept; the name is not, because a lower-case common noun in prose is a description, not an entity name, and every other object in this batch (Colorful Door, Rear Trap, Martello, Logging Point) is capitalised by its page. Bullet 7 is a pick-and-plant pair at one room ((I-9)/(J-8) to take a mature scourshroom, (I-9)/(J-9) to plant it) and bullet 8 says 'repeat the same process' at (E-7) without breaking out its two sub-locations, so each bullet is one rung and they share a group -- the page's own 'ensure that you have planted mature scourshrooms in both spots' is an unordered set, not a sequence.

No evidence anywhere in the mushroom half, and that is deliberate. The mature scourshroom is consumed by the planting and is not in any resource table; the harvest wants at least TWO young Scourshrooms, and the only thing 'Scourshroom' resolves to is key item 876 in the Temporary Key Items category -- a temporary key item, which the key-item packet does not report, and a count of two is not expressible for a key item in any case. Reaching for it would be exactly the kind of evidence hard rule 2 forbids, so the harvest step carries none and the requirement is recorded on the hand-in where it belongs.

Bullet 9's zone-and-wait folds into the harvest note rather than becoming an unmarkable rung between two steps on the same object, and bullet 12's 'clean twice, or five times for an extra Imperial Gold Piece' is a choice inside bullet 11's conversation, so those merge. The 04:00-06:00 game-time window and 'Complete 25 points worth of Assaults as Sergeant Major' are both real gates with nothing observable behind them. The header writes Abquhbah's grid as '(1-10)', a digit for the letter I.

notes:
The header names Kuchi Eyjhann in Valkurm Dunes as the giver, but bullet 1 is explicit that he is what you SEE, not what you touch: you examine the Cavernous Maw at (I-9) and 'you will receive a cutscene with Kuchi Eyjhann'. That is the Carbuncle Debacle shape exactly, so start moves to the Cavernous Maw -- a real, targetable entity in a resolved zone, where Kuchi Eyjhann is a cutscene actor who is not standing anywhere in Valkurm Dunes. The header string is kept verbatim in raw. This is a marker MOVE, not a removal.

'Traverser stone' is six key items sharing one name (res 1271-1276), so the resolver refuses to guess an id and stage C will drop the entry and mark the step partial. It is recorded anyway because it is a real and load-bearing precondition -- without a stone the Maw does nothing -- and an honest dropped entry is better than a silently missing requirement.

Bullet 2 is one line long and hands the entire spawn procedure off to the Abyssea - Misareaux page, naming no placeholder, no trigger item and no location, so the fight step carries the NM and nothing else; that incompleteness, not the ladder, is why this is medium. Bullet 3 is a real step but an odd one -- the closing cutscene fires on LEAVING the zone, and the page never says which zone you leave to, so the target is none rather than an invented destination. The nine-row reward table is a reward, never evidence: which abyssite you get depends only on how many Abyssea storyline quests you had already finished.
